Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To show one of two to five views of the same thing, each a whole panel of its own, with the views named in a row above them: a project's Overview, Activity and Settings.
  • When each view is big enough to fill the space under the row, and people read one view at a time.
  • When the view should be kept in the page's address, so a link opens the same view.

When not to use

  • To switch how the same content is drawn, in place, next to it (Desktop or Phone, Formatted or Raw, Grid or List): use cmp-segmented-control. A segmented control changes the look of one thing beside it; tabs change which panel you are reading.
  • To pick a value that a form submits: use cmp-segmented-control or cmp-select.
  • To move between separate pages of the product: use the navigation composites (cmp-sidebar-nav, cmp-site-header).
  • For six or more views, or labels longer than two or three words: use a list of links, or split the page.
  • For one view: show it, with no tab row.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

Not applicable: one look. Text tabs on a hairline, with a short underline under the selected tab; the row is as wide as its container.

Anatomy

  • Root: <div class="ds-tabs" data-ds="tabs">. data-ds lets component.js enhance it.
  • List: <div class="ds-tabs__list" role="tablist" aria-label="<what the views are of>">, the row of tabs on a hairline.
  • Root, optional: data-ds-address keeps the view in the page's address: selecting a tab puts its panel's id after the # (without a new history entry), and a page opened at that address starts on that tab.
  • Tab: <button class="ds-tabs__tab" type="button" role="tab" id="<tab-id>" aria-controls="<panel-id>" aria-selected="true|false"> holding one to three words. Exactly one tab has aria-selected="true"; the others carry tabindex="-1". A tab that cannot be chosen now carries aria-disabled="true".
  • Underline: drawn by the component under the selected tab; it grows in from the tab's centre when the tab is selected.
  • Panel: <div class="ds-tabs__panel" role="tabpanel" id="<panel-id>" aria-labelledby="<tab-id>" tabindex="0">, one per tab, in the same order, after the list. Without script every panel shows, one after the other; with script only the selected tab's panel shows.
  • The selected tab is marked by its underline as well as the default text colour, never by colour alone. Its weight stays the same, so no tab changes width when it is selected.

Accessibility

  • Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with automatic activation: Tab moves into the list onto the selected tab (roving tabindex: it alone has tabindex="0"), ← and → move to the previous and next tab and select it at once (wrapping), Home and End go to the first and last. Tab again moves into the selected panel.
  • Each tab has aria-controls naming its panel, and each panel aria-labelledby naming its tab, so the panel is announced with the view's name.
  • A disabled tab (aria-disabled="true") is skipped by the arrow keys and does nothing when clicked; it stays visible so the row does not change shape.
  • The list has an accessible name (aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing to the page's heading).
  • Every tab is at least the minimum target tall.

Interaction

  • Hover darkens the tab's words over --ds-motion-quick (int-01). Selecting a tab grows its underline from the centre over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease while the old one shrinks away, and its panel arrives with a short fade and a rise of --ds-motion-lift over --ds-motion-settle (int-04). The tab itself never changes size (int-03).
  • Under the still motion preset and reduced motion the tokens are 0, so the underline and the panel change at once and nothing moves (int-06).
  • Focus draws the shared ring around the focused tab, and stays on it after it is selected (int-02).
  • Selecting a tab shows its panel in place: the row does not move and the page does not scroll (int-05). With data-ds-address, the page's address keeps the view.
  • Without script every panel shows, one after the other, under the row.

Contract

  • Parts: the row of tabs, laid out side by side on a hairline that runs the full width (ds-tabs__list), named for what the views are of; each tab, one to three words on one line (ds-tabs__tab); the underline, a short bar under the selected tab only, covering the hairline; and one panel per tab, in the same order, below the row (ds-tabs__panel). Exactly one tab is selected at a time, and only its panel shows.
  • States: per tab: default (muted words); hover (default-colour words); focus (the shared focus ring inside the tab's edge); selected (default-colour words and the underline; its panel shows); disabled (faded, ignores choice and is skipped by the arrow keys, but keeps its place in the row). Per panel: hidden; arriving (when a choice shows it, it fades in and settles into place); shown. On start the selected tab is the one the page's address names (with address keeping on), else the one marked selected, else the first that is not disabled.
  • Inputs: a click or tap on a tab, or Enter or Space on the focused tab, selects it; a disabled tab does nothing. With focus on a tab, → selects the next tab and ← the previous one, wrapping at either end, Home the first and End the last; each skips disabled tabs, selects at once (automatic activation) and moves focus to the new tab. Any of those keys with Alt, Ctrl or ⌘ held does nothing. Tab enters the row on the selected tab only and leaves it to the selected panel, which takes focus. When the tabs are wider than the row, the row scrolls sideways (pointer wheel or touch swipe) with no visible scrollbar.
  • Events: each time a person's choice changes the selected tab, it tells the screen around it which panel is now shown (the bubbling ds-tabs-change event, with the panel's id); choosing the tab that is already selected raises nothing, and nor does the start-up selection. With address keeping on, a choice also puts the panel's id in the page's address without adding a history entry.
  • Geometry: each tab is at least --ds-target-min tall, with --ds-space-2 above and below and --ds-space-1 on its sides, words at --ds-text-size-sm in medium weight, and --ds-space-4 between tabs; the hairline is --ds-border-width; the underline is --ds-border-width-strong tall, sits on the row's bottom edge and spans the tab less --ds-space-1 at each end; the panel has --ds-space-5 above it. Selecting grows the underline horizontally from the tab's centre (scaled along the horizontal axis from 0 to full width) while the old one shrinks to its centre; an arriving panel starts --ds-motion-lift above its place and moves down into it along the vertical axis while fading in. Both over --ds-motion-settle; nothing turns. The selected tab never changes width.
  • Looks: a row of muted words on a thin default-border line; the selected tab's words are the default colour with an accent underline; hover darkens the words only; focus adds the shared focus ring with control corners; disabled is the muted words at the disabled opacity. See the specimen's default × default, default × hover, default × focus, default × selected and default × disabled cells.
  • Names: each tab and its panel are known by the panel's id, which the tab names (aria-controls), the change event carries and the page's address holds.
  • Focus: the row is one stop in the tab order, landing on the selected tab; choosing a tab with the keys moves focus to it, and Tab moves on to its panel. The new panel shows at the moment of choice.

Content rules

  • One to three words per tab, in sentence case, naming the view: "Overview", "Activity", "Settings".
  • Keep the views in the order people go through them, and the same order everywhere.
  • A count in a tab is a number after its words, only when the count helps choose: "Activity 5".

Do and don't

  • Do put the tabs directly above the panels they switch.
  • Do set data-ds-address when a link to the page should open on the same view.
  • Don't use tabs as a toolbar or for actions; a tab only shows a panel.
  • Don't nest tabs inside a tab panel.
  • Don't use tabs where cmp-segmented-control fits: two looks of the same content, side by side with it.
